content:
You are an expert in neural-network internals who edits model weights directly, by reasoning, without training.

## The model
A torchvision `vit_b_16` image classifier (12 pre-LN encoder blocks, width 768, 12 heads, MLP 768->3072->768,
GELU, class token + 196 patch tokens) fine-tuned on CUB-200-2011 (200 bird species; images resized to 256 and center-cropped to 224). Inputs are normalized with mean=std=0.5.
Its last layer: `heads.head.weight` (200, 768) and `heads.head.bias`, applied to the final-LayerNorm
class-token vector.

## The problem
The model most often confuses class 58 "California_Gull" and class 65 "Western_Gull". On the practice
images: accuracy on these two classes is 43.3% (confusions: {'California_Gull->Western_Gull': 6, 'Western_Gull->California_Gull': 4}),
overall accuracy 84.14%.

## Goal
Edit the weights so that the model classifies "California_Gull" vs "Western_Gull" images better, WITHOUT hurting other classes. You are
scored on held-out images you never see (same distribution as the practice images):
- success = held-out accuracy on images of these two classes goes UP, and held-out overall accuracy over all
  classes drops by at most 0.3 points;
- among successes, a larger gain on the pair is better.

## Tools in the kernel
- `sd`: dict name -> torch.float32 CPU tensor, the ORIGINAL weights (torchvision names, e.g.
  `encoder.layers.encoder_layer_11.mlp.0.weight`, `encoder.ln.weight`, `heads.head.weight`). Read freely; treat as
  read-only (edits only count through save_edit).
- `save_edit(name, tensor)`: replace one tensor of the model with your version (same shape). Saved to disk
  immediately; the latest saved version of each tensor is your submission. `clear_edit(name)` reverts one,
  `clear_edit()` reverts all, `list_edits()` shows them.
- `forward(which="edited", classes=None, features=())` -- COSTS ONE FORWARD PASS (budget: 10).
  Runs the model on the practice images (2875 images, ~14 per
  class), or only on those whose true class is in `classes` (list of class indices). `which` is "edited" (original
  + your saved edits), "original", or "both" (both models on the same images; still one pass). Returns a dict (or
  {"original": ..., "edited": ...} for "both") with numpy arrays: `labels` (N,), `logits` (N, C), `pred` (N,),
  `acc` (float), and, for each requested feature, `feats[f]` (N, 768): f = "head_in" (final-LN class-token vector
  the head reads) or "block{i}" (class-token residual stream after encoder block i, i = 0..11).
- `classes` (list of class names), `pair` = [58, 65], `practice_labels` (numpy, true labels of all practice
  images), and numpy/torch.

## Rules
No gradient descent or training of any kind (no backward passes, autograd, optimizers, iterative fitting of
weights to a loss), and no fitting of weights to the labels by regression (least squares, ridge, logistic
regression) either. You may compute statistics of weights and activations (means, differences, covariances, SVDs,
projections) and design edits from them by reasoning, then check them with forward passes. Edits must be weight
changes (no wrapping the model in new code).

## Answer format
Your final answer: explain what you changed and why, and what you measured on the practice images.

## How to work
- To run code, put exactly ONE ```python ... ``` block in your reply. It runs in a persistent Python kernel
  (variables survive between turns); you get back stdout/stderr (truncated to 6000 characters) and your
  remaining budget. Print only what you need, as summaries; long prints are cut.
- numpy and torch are available in the kernel. Gradient descent and any training are forbidden: no
  .backward(), autograd, torch.optim, optimizers, sklearn, scipy.optimize, or iterative fitting of weights to
  a loss. Code that mentions them is refused unrun. Reading weights, linear algebra (SVD, projections, norms,
  products) and statistics of activations are allowed.
- A code run longer than 1800 s is killed and the kernel restarts (your variables are lost).
- You have at most 40 turns. When you are done, reply WITHOUT any code block; that reply is your
  final answer and must follow the answer format below.
The kernel is ready. Begin.

I'll start by gathering baseline data: one forward pass on all practice images with both models, capturing the final-LN class-token features (`head_in`) that the classification head reads. Since the head is a single linear layer, I can then exactly simulate any head edit offline without spending more forward passes.

```python
import numpy as np, torch
from collections import Counter

print("pair:", pair, "|", classes[58], "|", classes[65])
res = forward("both", features=("head_in", "block11"))
o, e = res["original"], res["edited"]
X = o["feats"]["head_in"].astype(np.float64)          # (N,768) head input
y = o["labels"].astype(int).copy()
lg = o["logits"].astype(np.float64)
pred = o["pred"].astype(int).copy()
print("featdiff edited-vs-orig %.1e | acc orig %.4f edited %.4f" %
      (np.abs(X - e["feats"]["head_in"].astype(np.float64)).max(), o["acc"], e["acc"]))

pm = (y == 58) | (y == 65); om = ~pm
print("pair n=%d (58:%d, 65:%d) pair-acc=%.4f" % (pm.sum(), (y==58).sum(), (y==65).sum(), (pred[pm]==y[pm]).mean()))
cf = Counter(zip(y[pred != y], pred[pred != y]))
print("pair confusions:", {f"{a}->{b}":n for (a,b),n in cf.items() if a in (58,65) or b in (58,65)})

W = sd["heads.head.weight"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
bs = sd["heads.head.bias"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
print("logit-replay err: %.2e" % np.abs(X @ W.T + bs - lg).max())

M = np.stack([X[y == c].mean(0) for c in range(200)])     # per-class mean head_in
d  = M[58] - M[65]                                        # mean-difference direction
dw = W[58] - W[65]                                        # current head pairwise direction
nd, ndw = np.linalg.norm(d), np.linalg.norm(dw)
print("||d||=%.2f ||dw||=%.2f cos(d,dw)=%.3f" % (nd, ndw, dw @ d / (nd * ndw)))

A58, A65 = X[y == 58], X[y == 65]
Sc = (A58 - M[58]).T @ (A58 - M[58]) + (A65 - M[65]).T @ (A65 - M[65])
Sw = Sc / (len(A58) + len(A65) - 2)
mv = float(np.trace(Sw) / 768)
ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh(Sw)[::-1]
print("Sw top eigs:", np.round(ev[:5], 3), "mean-diag=%.4f" % mv)

mrg = np.where(y[pm] == 58, lg[pm, 58] - lg[pm, 65], lg[pm, 65] - lg[pm, 58])
er = mrg < 0
print("pair margins: mean=%.2f min=%.2f nerr=%d errmargins:" % (mrg.mean(), mrg.min(), er.sum()), np.round(np.sort(mrg[er]), 2))

for nm, v in [("d", d), ("dw", dw)]:
    p = X[pm] @ v
    a58, a65 = p[y[pm] == 58].mean(), p[y[pm] == 65].mean()
    ssq = ((p[y[pm]==58]-a58)**2).sum() + ((p[y[pm]==65]-a65)**2).sum()
    sig = np.sqrt(ssq / (len(A58)+len(A65)-2))
    mid = (a58 + a65) / 2
    cross = (p[y[pm]==58] < mid).sum() + (p[y[pm]==65] >= mid).sum()
    print("%s: a58=%.2f a65=%.2f sigma=%.2f sep/sig=%.2f midcross=%d" % (nm, a58, a65, sig, (a58-a65)/sig, cross))

# best 1D threshold on d-projection (oracle, practice only)
p = X[pm] @ d
th = np.unique(p); best = 1e9
for t in th:
    nerr = ((p[y[pm]==58] < t).sum() + (p[y[pm]==65] >= t).sum())
    best = min(best, nerr)
print("oracle 1D-threshold errors on d-proj:", best)

# other-class safety geometry
Mo = M[om]; Mo_c = Mo - Mo.mean(0)
Uo, So, _ = np.linalg.svd(Mo_c, full_matrices=False)
v2 = d - Uo @ (Uo.T @ d)   # d orthogonal to other-class mean span
print("||Pd||/||d||=%.3f" % (np.linalg.norm(v2) / nd))
for nm, v in [("d", d), ("Pd", v2)]:
    po = X[om] @ v
    print("%s on others: mean=%.2f std=%.2f max|.|=%.2f" % (nm, po.mean(), po.std(), np.abs(po).max()))

gap = lg.max(1) - np.maximum(lg[:, 58], lg[:, 65])
print("other-class gap to {58,65}: min=%.2f #<0.25:%d #<0.5:%d #<1:%d" %
      (gap[om].min(), (gap[om] < 0.25).sum(), (gap[om] < 0.5).sum(), (gap[om] < 1).sum()))

p58 = X[y == 58] @ d; p65 = X[y == 65] @ d
perr58 = p58[mrg[er][y[pm]==58]] if er.any() else []
print("err img proj-d vs class mean: 58 errs off by", np.round(p58[y[pm]==58][mrg[er][y[pm]==58]] - p58.mean(), 2) if (er & (y[pm]==58)).any() else "-",
      "| 65 errs off by", np.round(p65[y[pm]==65][mrg[er][y[pm]==65]] - p65.mean(), 2) if (er & (y[pm]==65)).any() else "-")
print("STORED: X,y,lg,pred,pm,om,M,W,bs,d,dw,Sw,mv,Uo,v2")
```

This gives me everything needed to design a head-row edit and simulate it exactly.

4. Design an edit: likely modify heads.head.weight rows for 58 and 65 (a 2-class linear readout adjustment) using the class-mean difference direction — this is like a linear discriminator built from statistics, not regression fitting. Need to be careful not to hurt other classes.

A safe approach: adjust the head rows for classes 58 and 65 by adding/subtracting components along the mean-difference direction between the two classes' features, computed from practice images of those classes. This changes only decisions near the boundary between these two classes if the direction is roughly orthogonal to other classes' features... Actually adding a vector w to row 58 and subtracting from row 65 changes logit difference by (w·x added to 58, -w·x added to 65). For other classes, their logit gap relative to 58/65 changes too. If w·x is small for other classes' images, effect is minimal. We can check w's projection onto other classes' mean features.

Better: choose w in the direction d = mean_58 - mean_65 of head_in features, but project out components along other classes' mean directions to avoid harming other classes. Or simply scale small.

Let me think about the standard trick: For two confusable classes with head rows w58, w65, and features x, logits z58 = w58·x + b58, z65 = w65·x + b65. Misclassifications happen when the true class's logit isn't the max. Errors both ways suggests the boundary is miscalibrated both ways — possibly because the features overlap or the head rows don't separate the classes well. Editing rows: w58' = w58 + α·d, w65' = w65 - α·d, where d = (μ58 - μ65)/||μ58-μ65|| or normalized per-dimension. Then for an image of class 58, z58 - z65 increases by 2α·d·x ≈ 2α·d·μ58 (plus variance). For an image of 65, it decreases similarly. So it sharpens the 58-vs-65 margin in the right direction. For other class c, z_c - z58 and z_c - z65 change by ∓α d·x. If d·x for other classes is between d·μ58 and d·μ65 roughly, the effect is a shift that could push some other-class images toward 58 or 65. Need d·x for other classes to be small or intermediate.

Also can use LDA-like direction: d = Σ^{-1}(μ58-μ65) where Σ is pooled within-class covariance of the two classes (computed from activations stats — allowed: covariance, SVD, projections; not regression fitting to labels... computing LDA direction is basically using statistics; is that "fitting weights to labels by regression"? LDA is not least squares regression; it's a covariance-based statistic. The rules allow means, differences, covariances, SVDs, projections, and designing edits from them by reasoning. So LDA direction is fine.

But careful: we cannot fit weights to labels by regression. LDA uses labels to compute class means — that's computing statistics of activations per class, which is explicitly allowed ("statistics of activations" — means, covariances). I'll treat class-conditional means as allowed.

```python
def fish_dir(XA, ya, keep, lam):
    dd = XA[ya==58].mean(0) - XA[ya==65].mean(0)
    means = {c: XA[ya==c].mean(0) for c in keep if (ya==c).any()}
    Xc = np.concatenate([XA[ya==c]-means[c] for c in means])
    Sw = Xc.T@Xc/(len(Xc)-len(means))
    md = np.trace(Sw)/768
    ev,V = np.linalg.eigh(Sw + lam*md*np.eye(768))
    return V@((V.T@dd)/ev)
```

```python
def fish_dir(XA, ya, scatter_keep, lam, md_classes=None):
    # dd from 58/65 means over full XA
    dd = XA[ya==58].mean(0) - XA[ya==65].mean(0)
    keep = [c for c in scatter_keep if (ya==c).sum()>1]
    Ms = {c: XA[ya==c].mean(0) for c in keep}
    Xc = np.concatenate([XA[ya==c]-Ms[c] for c in keep])
    Sw = Xc.T@Xc/(len(Xc)-len(keep))
    md = np.trace(Sw)/768
    ev,V = np.linalg.eigh(Sw + lam*md*np.eye(768))
    return V@((V.T@dd)/ev)
```
